text:
The dead do not need aspirin

or pity.

I suppose.


But maybe they need rain

Not shoes,

but a place to walk.


Not cigarettes,

they tell us,

but a place to burn.


Or we have been told:

space and a place to fly

may be the same thing.


The dead do not need me.

Nor do the living.


But maybe the dead need

themselves.


In fact, the dead maybe

need everything

we need.


And we need so much.

If only we knew what.


Maybe it is everything.


And we will probably die

trying to get it.


Or we will die

because we do not get it.


I hope you understand,

when I am dead


That I got

as much as I could.

translation.title: The Dead Do Not Need Aspirin...
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the speculative, stripped meditation on what the dead and living need.
